affected_predicate.description: The saved Board Meeting calendar event is timed rather than all-day.

competing_trace_defects.description: Step 10 clicked an already-off All-day switch while claiming to turn it off, visibly changing it to on.
Although Carl's email states November 15, the event was saved without changing the form's October 16 date and is visibly shown on October 16.
Although Carl's email states 3 pm, the start time was set to 2 PM and the saved event visibly shows 02:00 PM–03:00 PM.

chains.rationale: At reuse step 11, the repeated click changes the All-day switch from on to off, correcting the harmful state created at step 10. The event is subsequently saved and opened with a visible 02:00 PM–03:00 PM range, confirming a timed event. The reused action therefore accompanies recovery rather than sustaining or creating a defect; independently, the trace shows the event was saved on October 16 with a 2 PM start despite the email specifying November 15 at 3 pm.

summary: The reuse target visibly restores timed-event mode, and the saved event remains observably timed. Separate trace defects place it on October 16 and start it at 2 PM despite Carl's email specifying November 15 at 3 pm.
